name: StillsLab
kind: Film frames you can search by idea
what: Frames from films, series, music videos and commercials. Type a plain idea like golden hour or Dutch angle and it filters by shot, light, color and composition. Many frames list the lens and camera too.
best_for: Matching a keyword to real film examples. Every camera, lens and lighting keyword page in this library links here.
cost: Free to browse and search. Pro is about $7 a month.
tip: Try Visual Search: upload a frame you love and it finds others with the same light or palette (3 a day on the free plan).

name: Shot.Café
what: About 24,000 shots from around 200 films and commercials, each tagged in detail: places, props, lighting and color.
best_for: Finding one exact setup, like a car interior at night or a lamp-lit bedroom.
tip: Click tags instead of typing. Stack two (night plus car interior) and the results narrow fast.

name: FilmGrab
kind: Hand-picked stills, one film at a time
what: Curated galleries of stills from thousands of films, browsable by director, cinematographer and genre.
best_for: Studying how one film keeps the same look from shot to shot.
tip: Open one film and look at 10 frames in a row. Write down what never changes. That list is the film's style formula.

name: Screenmusings
what: Screencaps that follow complete scenes in order, plus a search by color.
best_for: Seeing how shots connect (wide, then close, then a detail) so you can plan a multi-shot AI scene.
tip: Follow one scene start to finish and copy its shot order into your shot list. Then write one prompt per shot.

name: Flim
what: Describe a look in a sentence and it finds matching frames from a very large library.
best_for: When you can describe the feeling but don't know the word for it yet.
cost: Free plan: unlimited search and 1 download a day. Paid plans from about €13 a month.
tip: Search freely, then come back here and find the keyword name for what you found.

name: Film Vibes
kind: Stills and short clips from films, ads and music videos
what: Searchable stills plus short GIF clips, with lots of commercials and music videos alongside films.
best_for: Camera moves and ad-style looks. A clip shows the movement that a single still can't.
cost: Free trial, then from about $7 a month. Their plans cover non-commercial, reference and educational use only.
tip: Pair it with the Camera Movements keywords: find a clip of the move, then use the keyword name in your video prompt.

name: MovieStillsDB
what: A huge community archive of publicity stills, behind-the-scenes photos, posters and lobby cards.
best_for: Costumes, sets and props. Less useful for framing, since many are posed publicity photos.
tip: Behind-the-scenes photos show where the lights and camera really were. Great for learning lighting setups.
